events.title: Bauernmarkt am Karmelitermarkt
events.description: One of Vienna’s biggest farmers’ markets, across the canal from the old town in Leopoldstadt. Regional meat, sausage and seasonal fruit and vegetables.
events.why: A neighbourhood market where locals actually shop, with good cafés around the square.

events.title: Flohmarkt am Naschmarkt
events.description: Vienna’s big weekly flea market, at the far end of the Naschmarkt food market. Old furniture, records, glassware, postcards and plenty of junk.
events.why: A real Saturday-morning habit for locals. Go early for the best finds, then have breakfast at one of the market’s cafés.

events.title: Biomarkt Freyung
events.description: A small organic farmers’ market on a square in the old town, selling bread, cheese, vegetables and other local produce.
events.why: An easy, low-key look at what Austrian farmers grow, right in the centre. Good for picnic food.

events.title: Bernhard Leitner: SOUNDSPACESCULPTURE
events.description: An exhibition where sound is the material: a Viennese artist uses speakers and moving sound to shape the space you walk through. Two other artists show alongside him.
events.why: Last chance. The same ticket gets you into the basement room with Klimt’s Beethoven Frieze, a famous wall painting from 1902.

events.title: Erika Giovanna Klien: All Is Movement
events.description: Paintings and drawings by a Viennese artist of the 1920s who tried to show movement and speed on paper and canvas, part of a short-lived local avant-garde.
events.why: A side of 1920s Vienna few visitors see, a short walk through the garden from the Belvedere’s famous Klimts.

events.title: Viennale
events.description: Vienna’s big film festival: two weeks of new films from around the world, an old-Hollywood retrospective, talks with filmmakers and late-night parties.
events.why: The city’s main cultural event of the autumn. If a screening is sold out, check the festival’s page for returned tickets.

events.title: Robert Aldrich retrospective
events.description: A season of tough, stylish Hollywood films from the 1950s to the 1970s by one director, including the war film The Dirty Dozen, at the city’s film museum.
events.why: Many screenings start with a short live introduction, and the season runs on for weeks after the festival.
events.dateNote: What Ever Happened to Baby Jane? Nov 21 · The Dirty Dozen Nov 22

events.title: MAK Day 2026
events.description: Free entry all day to the museum of design and decorative arts on the national holiday, including its rooms of Vienna 1900 furniture and glass.
events.why: A free way into one of the city’s best museums on a day when many shops are shut.

events.title: Vienna 1900: guided tour in English
events.description: A guided tour in English through rooms of Viennese furniture, glass and household design from around 1900, when the city set new standards for modern design.
events.why: An easy, guided way into Vienna 1900 design, with someone to explain what you’re looking at.

events.title: Nationalfeiertag
events.description: Austria’s national holiday. The army usually sets up displays on Heldenplatz, the big square by the old palace, and police and fire services show their work at City Hall.
events.why: This is how Viennese families spend the day, strolling among tanks and fire engines. Many shops are closed today.

events.title: Otello
events.description: Verdi’s opera of Shakespeare’s Othello, a story of jealousy and betrayal, with Jonas Kaufmann, one of the world’s best-known tenors, in the title role.
events.why: A chance to hear one of opera’s biggest names in one of Verdi’s greatest dramas. Seats go fast.
events.language: Sung in Italian, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Nijinsky
events.description: A new ballet about Vaslav Nijinsky, a famous early 20th-century dancer whose career ended in mental illness. Told through big, dramatic dancing.
events.why: The State Ballet’s big new show of the autumn. You don’t need any words to follow it.

events.title: Wir sind noch einmal davongekommen
events.description: Thornton Wilder’s The Skin of Our Teeth, an American comedy about one family that survives the ice age, a great flood and war, played in German.
events.why: A play many English speakers know, so it’s easy to follow, with subtitles on your phone.
events.language: In German, with phone subtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: Chicago
events.language: In German with the songs in English, German and English subtitles
events.description: The Broadway musical about two murderesses in 1920s Chicago who turn their trials into a show. Sharp, jazzy songs and lots of dancing.
events.why: A brand-new production, and the songs stay in English, so it’s easy to follow.

events.title: Das Ferienhaus
events.description: A modern family drama based on a classic play by Ibsen, set at a holiday house, on the main stage of Vienna’s national theatre.
events.why: One of the few evenings at the national theatre where you can follow along with subtitles on your phone.
events.language: In German, with phone subtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: Der fliegende Holländer
events.description: Wagner’s opera The Flying Dutchman: a ghostly sea captain is doomed to sail forever unless a woman stays faithful to him. Stormy, dramatic music.
events.why: Wagner in a small, historic theatre, much closer to the stage than at the big State Opera.
events.language: Sung in German, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: L’Orfeo
events.description: One of the very first operas ever written, from 1607: the myth of Orpheus, who goes down to the underworld to bring back his dead wife.
events.why: A chance to hear how opera began, in one of the world’s grandest opera houses.
events.language: Sung in Italian, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Die letzten Tage der Menschheit
events.description: A huge, biting satire of Vienna during the First World War, “The Last Days of Mankind”, written by the city’s most famous critic and long thought impossible to stage.
events.why: A big Viennese classic, made easier with phone subtitles, and some €25 tickets on Oct 30.
events.language: In German, with phone subtitles (English not confirmed)

events.title: Wiener Konzerthaus Backstage Tour in English
events.description: A guided tour behind the scenes of the Konzerthaus, one of the city’s two great concert halls, built in 1913.
events.why: A cheap, daytime look at the halls and backstage areas, in English.

events.title: Wien Modern
events.description: A month of new and experimental music in concert halls, clubs and churches around the city. Expect anything from orchestras to sound installations.
events.why: A different side of musical Vienna, often in unusual places, with top orchestras and ensembles.

events.title: Sonntagsmesse in der Hofburgkapelle
events.titleEnglish: Sunday mass with the Vienna Boys’ Choir
events.venueNote: the chapel in the old palace
events.description: The famous boys’ choir sings Sunday mass in the small royal chapel of the Hofburg, the old imperial palace. On Nov 15 and 29 the Vienna Choir Girls sing instead.
events.why: The way to hear the choir where it has sung for centuries, as part of a real church service rather than a concert.

events.title: La Fille du régiment
events.description: A comic opera about a girl raised by a regiment of soldiers. It’s short, funny and a gentle first opera.
events.why: A light evening if you’ve never been to an opera, and an easy break from the heavier works this month.
events.language: Sung in French, subtitles not confirmed

events.title: Talk with Volker Schlöndorff
events.description: A talk with Volker Schlöndorff, the German director of The Tin Drum, a 1979 film that won both the top prize at Cannes and an Oscar.
events.why: A chance to hear a key figure of German film in person.
events.venueNote: festival centre in the old radio building

events.title: Ernst Molden & Der Nino aus Wien
events.description: Two Viennese songwriters, one older and one younger, singing their own songs about Austria in the local dialect, in the tradition of the Wienerlied (Viennese song).
events.why: Music that locals actually listen to, in a proper concert hall.

events.title: Bill Frisell Trio
events.description: A trio led by an American jazz guitarist who blends jazz with country and folk. Warm, melodic music, mostly without words.
events.why: A guitarist who usually plays much bigger halls, in Vienna’s main jazz club.

events.title: Blickfang
events.description: A design fair where about 160 selected designers sell their own furniture, lamps, clothes and jewellery, at the museum of design and decorative arts.
events.why: You can buy straight from the people who made it, and chat with them while you do.

events.title: Franz West: The Revolution of Sculpture
events.description: A big show of a Viennese artist known for lumpy, odd sculptures you were often allowed to sit on or handle, at the modern branch of the Albertina museum.
events.why: The autumn’s big exhibition on one of Vienna’s own artists, opening this week.

events.title: Pygmalion / Pichon: Mozart Messe c-moll
events.titleEnglish: Mozart’s Great Mass in C minor
events.description: Mozart’s grandest piece of church music, for choir, soloists and orchestra, played by a French period-instrument group.
events.why: Big, joyful Mozart in the hall where Vienna goes for its serious concerts.

events.title: Vienna Art Week
events.description: A week of free tours, talks, open studios and exhibitions with around 70 museums, galleries and art schools across the city.
events.why: It’s free, and the open studio days get you into artists’ workspaces you couldn’t otherwise see.

events.title: Christmas Market at Schönbrunn Palace
events.description: A Christmas market in front of Schönbrunn, the emperors’ summer palace, and one of the first in the city to open.
events.why: Opens before most other markets, so you get the mulled wine and the palace view without the December crowds.

events.title: KlezMORE Festival
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: A week of klezmer, the dance and party music of Jewish Eastern Europe, with concerts, readings and films around the city.
events.why: A lively side of Vienna’s Jewish culture, in small venues where locals go.

events.title: Lise Davidsen sings Schubert
events.description: Lise Davidsen, one of today’s most talked-about opera singers, sings Schubert’s songs with piano, in Vienna’s grand concert hall.
events.why: A huge opera voice in an intimate set of songs, in the city where Schubert wrote them.

events.title: Art&Antique
events.description: An art and antiques fair with dealers from Austria and abroad, from ancient objects to modern design, inside the old imperial palace.
events.why: A chance to browse old Viennese furniture and design in the palace’s grand halls, whether or not you buy.

events.title: Viennese Christmas Market at Rathausplatz
events.description: The city’s biggest Christmas market, in front of the City Hall, with skating paths winding through the park beside it.
events.why: Go in the first week, before the coach tours arrive.
events.dateNote: Opens Nov 13 · Ice rink until Jan 6

events.title: Weihnachtsmarkt am Spittelberg
events.description: Craft stalls set up in the narrow old lanes of Spittelberg, a quarter of small 1700s and 1800s houses just behind the museum district.
events.why: The Christmas market locals tend to prefer: more crafts, less kitsch, and pretty streets.

events.title: Old Viennese Christmas Market
events.description: A traditional Christmas market on an old square in the centre, selling handmade crafts, glass ornaments, nativity figures and pottery.
events.why: The old-fashioned choice in the city centre, with live Christmas music in the late afternoons.

events.title: Madama Butterfly
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s heartbreaking opera about a young Japanese woman who waits years for the American naval officer who married her and left.
events.why: One of the most moving and tuneful operas, and a good first one.

events.title: Blue Bird 2026
events.description: Three nights of singer-songwriters, four acts a night, from Austria, Ireland, Scandinavia and Britain, at the city’s main jazz club.
events.why: A relaxed way to hear new songwriters up close, in a club with good sound.

events.title: Royal Concertgebouworkest / Klaus Mäkelä
events.dateNote: Also Nov 20, with a different programme
events.description: Amsterdam’s famous orchestra on tour, playing a Mahler symphony on the first night and Dvořák and Bartók on the second.
events.why: One of the world’s top orchestras in one of the best-sounding halls anywhere.

events.title: Ariadne auf Naxos
events.language: Sung in German. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Richard Strauss’s opera about a rich man who orders a tragic opera and a comedy troupe to perform at the same time. Funny first half, glowing music in the second.
events.why: The State Opera’s new production of the season, led by Vienna-born conductor Franz Welser-Möst.

events.title: Berliner Skulpturenfund: Entartete Kunst im Bombenschutt
events.titleEnglish: The Berlin Sculpture Find: “Degenerate Art” in the Bomb Rubble
events.description: Modernist sculptures the Nazis condemned as “degenerate art”, which turned up decades later in wartime bomb rubble in central Berlin.
events.why: A small, surprising story of Berlin’s buried past. Closes this Sunday.

events.title: Ruin and Rush: Berlin 1910–1930
events.description: Painting and art from Berlin between the First World War and the end of the 1920s, when the city was broke, wild and full of new ideas.
events.why: The Berlin of Babylon Berlin and Cabaret, seen through the artists who lived it.

events.title: The Opposite of Now: Artistic Paths to a Different Present
events.dateNote: Last chance! Closes on Nov 22 · Closed Mondays and Sat Nov 14
events.description: A group show of contemporary art imagining other ways the present could look, inside Daniel Libeskind’s zigzag museum building.
events.why: Last weeks of the show, and the building itself is worth the trip.

events.title: Kreuzberg: Kunst und Migration seit 1960
events.description: Art about the guest workers from Turkey, Greece and Italy who moved to Kreuzberg from the 1960s, and how they changed the district.
events.why: Explains the Kreuzberg you see today, in a museum on its edge. Walk out into the neighbourhood after.

events.title: Ryuichi Sakamoto: seeing sound, hearing time
events.venueNote: contemporary art museum in a former railway station
events.description: Sound and video installations by the late Japanese composer behind the music for The Last Emperor and Merry Christmas, Mr. Lawrence.
events.why: An exhibition you listen to as much as look at, in a beautiful old station hall.

events.title: Carrie Mae Weems: The Heart of the Matter
events.venueNote: photography centre in the Amerika Haus by Zoo station
events.description: Photographs by an American artist known for her Kitchen Table Series, quiet staged pictures about family, race and power.
events.why: Berlin’s leading photography venue, showing one of the most important living photographers.

events.title: Christoph Schlingensief: Es ist nicht mehr mein Problem, macht eure Scheiße alleine
events.titleEnglish: Christoph Schlingensief: It’s Not My Problem Anymore, Deal With Your Own Shit
events.description: The biggest show in over a decade on a German provocateur who worked across film, theatre, opera and political stunts until his death in 2010.
events.why: A way into the angry, funny side of German culture after reunification.

events.title: Portraits! Surprising Encounters from Botticelli to Lempicka
events.description: Six centuries of portraits, from Botticelli, Dürer and Rubens to 1920s painter Tamara de Lempicka, hung in unexpected pairs.
events.why: New this month, and the old-masters gallery is rarely crowded.

events.title: Genghis Khan and the World of the Mongols
events.description: A big new exhibition on Genghis Khan and the vast Mongol empire he founded in the 1200s.
events.why: Just opened, and a good reason to see the new entrance building on Museum Island.

events.title: Josef Kaiser: Building for the GDR
events.description: The East German architect behind Karl-Marx-Allee’s Kino International cinema, Hotel Berolina and Restaurant Moskau, the modernist side of 1960s East Berlin.
events.why: See the show, then go and look at the real buildings, which still stand on Karl-Marx-Allee.

events.title: Just revolutionary – The Films of the Ninjin Club
events.dateNote: Kaidan Oct 31 at 20:00 with an introduction · Last chance! Ends Oct 31
events.description: A season of Japanese films from the 1950s and 60s made by a small company three actresses founded, including Kobayashi’s ghost-story film Kwaidan.
events.why: Rare prints of Japanese classics at Berlin’s main art-house cinema, most with English subtitles.

events.title: Street Food Thursday
events.description: Every Thursday evening a 19th-century market hall in Kreuzberg fills with food stalls from around the world, with beer from the hall’s own brewers.
events.why: A Berlin Thursday-night habit, busy with locals after work. Go hungry and early.

events.title: Wochenmarkt in der Markthalle Neun
events.description: The big market days at the Markthalle Neun: bakers, butchers, cheese makers and vegetable growers from around Berlin, plus cafés inside the hall.
events.why: Where Kreuzberg actually does its weekend shopping. Good for breakfast, bread and picnic food.

events.title: Flohmarkt im Mauerpark
events.description: Berlin’s best-known Sunday flea market, beside a park on the old Wall strip. Mostly private sellers with records, clothes, bikes, toys and furniture.
events.why: The classic Berlin Sunday: rummage, eat at the food stalls, then walk through the park where the Wall once ran.

events.title: Lunchkonzerte in der Philharmonie
events.titleEnglish: Free lunchtime concerts at the Philharmonie
events.description: A free 40–50 minute concert in the foyer of the home of the Berlin Philharmonic, usually chamber music or piano played by orchestra members and young players. Standing only.
events.why: The cheapest way inside the famous yellow concert hall. Come at least 45 minutes early: once the foyer is full, nobody else gets in.

events.title: Erinnerung eines Mädchens
events.description: A stage version of Annie Ernaux’s memoir about one summer in 1958, when she was 18, and how it marked the rest of her life.
events.why: A rare chance to see one of Germany’s leading theatres with English subtitles.

events.title: Tosca
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s thriller about a singer, her painter lover and the police chief who wants her. Big tunes and a short, gripping story.
events.why: A good first opera in the city’s grandest opera house on Unter den Linden, with seats from €10.

events.title: Jazzfest Berlin
events.venueNote: main venue, also clubs and a church around town
events.description: Four days of adventurous jazz from 24 bands, from American saxophone pioneer Anthony Braxton to Berlin’s free-jazz orchestra, at a festival theatre and smaller clubs.
events.why: One of Europe’s oldest jazz festivals, and the week Berlin’s jazz crowd comes out.

events.title: Konzerthausorchester Berlin: Brahms & Schumann
events.description: The resident orchestra plays Schumann’s cello concerto and Brahms’s Fourth Symphony, a dark and stormy favourite.
events.why: Classic orchestral music in a grand 1820s hall on Gendarmenmarkt, one of Berlin’s finest squares.

events.title: Orpheus in the Underworld
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Offenbach’s comic operetta that sends the gods of Olympus to a party in hell. Famous for the can-can.
events.why: A light, silly night out from a company known for wild, funny stagings.

events.title: Eugene Onegin
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Tchaikovsky’s opera about a bored young man who turns down a girl’s love letter and regrets it years later, in a staging full of summer countryside.
events.why: The Komische Oper is Berlin’s most playful opera company, and this is one of its best-loved productions.

events.title: Die bitteren Tränen der Petra von Kant
events.titleEnglish: The Bitter Tears of Petra von Kant
events.description: Fassbinder’s 1972 film about a fashion designer who falls hard for a young model. Set entirely in one stylish apartment.
events.why: A key film by the wild man of 1970s German cinema, shown with English subtitles.

events.title: Berlin Science Week
events.description: Ten days of talks, debates and open labs with scientists all over the city, hundreds of them free.
events.why: Many events are in English and free, so it’s an easy way to meet the city’s researchers.

events.title: Mononoke
events.language: With English subtitles (spoken language not confirmed)
events.description: A new piece by Japanese playwright and director Satoko Ichihara, known for strange, funny and unsettling plays about bodies and desire.
events.why: Experimental theatre you can follow in English at the Volksbühne, the city’s most rebellious playhouse.

events.title: Der Teich
events.description: A dark, dreamlike family drama based on a short play by the Swiss writer Robert Walser, staged by French director Gisèle Vienne.
events.why: Two nights only, performed in English, by one of Europe’s most talked-about theatre makers.

events.title: Heissa Holzmarkt
events.description: An alternative Christmas market in a creative village right on the Spree, with a varied programme and a big choice of food.
events.why: The early, laid-back alternative to the big Christmas markets. Open Wednesday to Sunday.

events.title: Wunderkammer
events.dateNote: Also Nov 8 at 18:00 · Last performance Nov 8
events.description: A dance piece by Spanish choreographer Marcos Morau, whose shows look like moving surrealist paintings.
events.why: Striking to look at and needs no words. Only two performances left.

events.title: Eröffnungskonzert Barocktage 2026
events.language: Sung in Italian. Subtitles not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Love songs and laments from 1600s Italy, including Monteverdi, played on old instruments, with the tenor Rolando Villazón as a narrator and singer.
events.why: The opening night of the opera house’s yearly baroque festival, with seats from €9.

events.title: Cheese Berlin
events.description: A one-day cheese market with small producers selling and offering tastings in the Markthalle Neun.
events.why: A Sunday outing in a hall that is normally closed on Sundays.

events.title: Hamlet
events.description: A new German version of Shakespeare’s play about a prince who can’t decide whether to avenge his murdered father.
events.why: A play you probably know, at Brecht’s old theatre, with English subtitles on this night.

events.title: INTERFILM 42
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Berlin’s short film festival, with screenings, talks and late-night programmes such as a long night of weird shorts.
events.why: Short films are an easy way to sample a lot of new cinema in one evening.

events.title: Weihnachtsmarkt an der Gedächtniskirche
events.titleEnglish: Christmas market at the Kaiser Wilhelm Memorial Church
events.description: One of the first big Christmas markets to open, around the bombed-out church tower that West Berlin kept as a war memorial.
events.why: The first chance this season for mulled wine at a proper Berlin Christmas market.

events.title: Festival nowHERE
events.dateNote: Opening walk-through concert Nov 13 at 18:00 and 21:00 · Closing concert Nov 21 at 20:00
events.description: A week of new music at the Konzerthaus. It opens with a concert you walk through, across three halls, with 88 musicians spread among the audience.
events.why: The closing night pairs Stravinsky’s Rite of Spring with a live electronic set, a very Berlin mix.

events.title: Ibrahim Maalouf & The Trumpets of Michel-Ange Vol. 2
events.description: A French-Lebanese trumpeter whose music mixes jazz with Arabic melodies, with his band.
events.why: A big-hearted, rhythmic concert in a classical hall, and easy to enjoy without knowing jazz.

events.title: Reading List Berlin: No. 1 with Katie Kitamura
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: An evening of conversation with the American novelist Katie Kitamura, author of Intimacies and Audition, at the Volksbühne.
events.why: A chance to hear a much-read contemporary novelist in person in a small room.

events.title: Winter Market Schlossplatz
events.venueNote: in front of the Humboldt Forum
events.description: A new winter market with crafts, food and old fairground rides in front of the rebuilt Berlin palace in the historic centre.
events.why: Easy to combine with Museum Island across the water.

events.title: Madama Butterfly
events.language: Language not confirmed, check before booking
events.description: Puccini’s opera about a young Japanese woman who waits years for the American naval officer who married her and left. A new production.
events.why: The first night of a new staging, with a party afterwards.

events.title: WeihnachtsZauber am Gendarmenmarkt
events.description: An upmarket Christmas market of white tents on one of Berlin’s grandest squares, between two domed churches and the concert hall.
events.why: The prettiest setting of any Berlin Christmas market, and quieter in its first days.
